t: 3159. Find Occurrences of an Element in an Array
o: We must answer, for each query q, the index of the q-th occurrence of x in nums, or -1 if x occurs fewer than q times. In example 1, x=1 occurs at indices 0 and 2, so queries 1 and 3 map to 0 and 2 while queries 2 and 4 exceed the occurrence count and yield -1. Since values are up to 1e4 and lengths up to 1e5, a single preprocessing pass plus O(1) lookups per query is ideal.
k: Collect all indices of x once in a preprocessing pass; the k-th occurrence is simply the k-th element of that list.
Each query is then an O(1) array access with a bounds check.

a.i: Scan nums once and record every index where the value equals x, in order. Query q then corresponds directly to the (q-1)-th entry of this list; if q exceeds the list length, the answer is -1. This turns every query into constant time after linear preprocessing.
s: Build a list occ of all indices i with nums[i] == x.
For each query q, output occ[q-1] if q <= len(occ), otherwise -1.
a.t: O(n + Q) — one scan of nums plus O(1) per query
a.sp: O(n) for the occurrence index list in the worst case

w: This is the natural and optimal solution; anything per-query that rescans nums is unnecessary. Pitfalls: forgetting the -1 case and off-by-one on the q-th occurrence (use occ[q-1]). A follow-up might ask for the q-th occurrence in a stream — that would require online insertion into a dynamic list.
